newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen lower on softer crudes.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen lower on softer crudes.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Monday were assessed softer on lower crude prices, traders said.
They said China has yet to show any real buying interest after cutting fuel oil imports tariffs to three percent from 12 percent since November 11.
Traders noted that if China emerged to buy, South Korean sellers would offer aggressively.

They said talking levels on Monday would be about $1.00 below the deal done Friday at $119 a tonne between a U.S. major and a Singapore trader for an early-December cargo of 180-cst fuel oil, on a free-on-board basis.

Traders said state-run Korea Electric Power Co (KEPCO) plans to issue a term tender soon to buy 0.3-percent sulphur, 540-cst fuel oil for January-June 1997 deliveries. The tender would seek over 400,000 barrels of fuel oil a month, they said.

Traders also said Indonesia's monthly low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) export allocation from Indonesia lifting in December is expected to be known by next week. They expect the December allotment to be around 3.6-3.8 million barrels, around November's 3.6 million barrels.
Swaps levels edged lower with December quoted at $117.00/$118.00 about 50 cents to $1 below Friday's levels.
